meta.title: The Pintland Isles — Dynamics Simulator
meta.changes: global and regional hazards, three new town crises (Shanty Town, Roto, Fenwick), and regions for every group
sources: THE PINTLAND ISLES — MASTER LORE COMPENDIUM
A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Concept Economy)

groups.name: The Liquor Kings
groups.description: Seamus Bonehardy, Jack Anqoak, Jagerbauhm, Guinnie, Buke and Jameson Pilsner — the Parliament of the Liquor Kings. Heroes of the Cloister Beast, the MAA and Maximilian; also blamed for Thatcher's death, a massacre, an assassination and a mountain of Stewards-era debt. Legitimacy genuinely contested.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (The Liquor Kings); Concepts I–VI

groups.name: Aleforge Mayoral Government
groups.description: The Bonehardy Administration. Seamus won the mayoral election after Drake's banishment and "has since done absolutely nothing in his tenure" — a fact called out by the other Kings — yet the town is calm and mostly supportive. Inherited the crisis-era bond debt; still employs John Rump as treasurer.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Aleforge — Modern History); Hall of Records (Mayoral Election Speeches)

groups.name: Church of Patmos (Providence)
groups.description: One office, three powers: Cardinal Addy's spire is Providence's government, its market regulator (it decrees what may be crafted or sold) and its church. Tithes flow upward at half of all earnings. Scholars whisper that ClockHeart Tonic binds souls to the church's will.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Providence); VI (The Church of Patmos)

groups.name: Roto Kaiishi Merchant-Philosophers
groups.description: The floating city Xi Jin Ping founded as a fence for pirate plunder. No sales tax, a flat yearly merchant fee, taboos instead of laws, and a hand-picked chain of merchant-philosopher heirs (Kim Jong Un) meant to stop the biggest players writing the rules.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Shanty Town & the Windsunk Council
groups.description: Lawless cliff settlement beside Sackbeard's Tavern. The Windsunk Council "decide who eats, who raids, and who gets tossed off the cliffs." Tide Callers, Coral-eyed, the Ashen Oath, and every crew its own little nation. Skeptical of any centralized power — the Kings included.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Shanty Town; Political Factions; Foreign Relations)

groups.name: MAMA (Prohibitionist Insurgency)
groups.description: Heirs of the MAA (massacred by the Kings in a cave). Rose again as Mothers Against Maximilian's Assassination; secretly founded by Susan Plinket ("JR"). Plinket is sentenced to be Rollo's girlfriend and the cells are "rendered inoperable" — but the ideology that alcohol is moral corruption was never killed.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (The MAA / MAMA; Susan Plinket); Concept V

groups.name: Gideon Drake (Exiled)
groups.description: The Bastard Veil. Part-Veilwalker, Sackbeard's first mate and killer, former mayor who actually governed (Barley Road, subsidies, bonds, militia) — and John Cum's murderer, who framed MAMA for it. Banished to unexplored Vodkonia: long-lived, resourceful, desperate.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Gideon Drake); Concept V; XI (Open Mysteries)

groups.name: Aleforge Brewing & Export
groups.description: The Gilded Tankard's magic spring, Brewers Lane and Trials tourism — Aleforge is a single-export state and knows it. The Tankard's entire stockpile currently sits under Goldcoral control, sold in secret at Jack's Grog Galley.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Gilded Tankard); II (Aleforge)

groups.name: Goldcoral Incorporated
groups.description: "Aggressive mercantilism." Headquartered in Providence, but every real book is kept in Roto, where nobody asks. Privately owned by Jack Anqoak; seized the Gilded Tankard's stockpile after Wepple gambled the investment away.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (Goldcoral Incorporated)

groups.name: The Ducket (M2 Stability)
groups.description: The global inter-town trade currency; every town runs its own sub-economy and converts at exchange rates that move with story events. Total supply (M2) is meant to stay flat — almost nothing may create new Duckets, and the one feasible exception is an influx from an outside economy. Higher = a flatter, more trusted M2 and stabler conversion rates.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Global Currency; The Concept Economy)

groups.name: Ducket Velocity
groups.description: How fast Duckets change hands — the second number the Analysis tracks. "If M2 is flat and velocity is consistent after six months we're on the right track." Low velocity is coin buried in chests and a stalled economy; very high velocity on a flat M2 is inflation's other door.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Global Currency; To Those Drunk in the Back of the Room)

groups.name: Player Economy (Shops, Wages & Contracts)
groups.description: What the people of the Isles actually feel: shop stock and prices, restock rates, NPC wages, rotating town contracts. Driven top-down by the Concept Economy — players have little to no power over it. "As items get scarcer and more expensive, they feel that their town is struggling even if they don't know it's due to embargos." Shops restock with town prosperity, never below a floor.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Player Economy vs. Concept Economy)

groups.name: Banks & Credit
groups.description: The key intermediary between the player and concept economies: loans for land, ships and shops; holdings accounts paying small interest. The catch — that interest must come from loan income, never from minted coin. The credit market is young.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Banks and Insurance)

groups.name: Voyage Insurers
groups.description: Insurance began as a few people gambling on whether or not ships would return from voyages. "As unsexy as insurance is, gambling is smoking hot." Every Stormtide is claims season; every pirate raid is a payout.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Banks and Insurance)

groups.name: Roto Currency Black Market
groups.description: Where the posted exchange rates stop meaning anything. "A strong black market for currencies would be fun, obviously based in Roto" — and it fits Roto's taboo system exactly: not illegal, just sold after dark. Insider trading and arbitrage are features, not bugs.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Player Economy; Taxes and Treasuries); Compendium II (Roto Kaiishi)

groups.name: Aleforge Bond Market
groups.description: Instituted by Drake at low rates, expanded by the Kings during the Stewards crisis "at increasingly unfavorable interest rates." Roto traders are the big holders. Stat = market confidence; low values mean the debt is winning.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Aleforge Bond Market)

groups.name: The Cumstead Wheat Supply
groups.description: Aleforge's key grain source. Its plenty was the Veilwalker blessing on John Cum; Cum is dead (by Drake's hand), the fields saw blight and green Factory sludge, and John Rump — addict, embezzler — now holds it without the blessing.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (John Cum's Cumstead); Concept V

groups.name: Southern Bellows Nation (via StormVeil)
groups.description: The fog-wrapped, agnostic-by-law brewers of the worst IPAs in existence, only now cracking their isolation through illegal Ale Bean routes and a partnership with StormVeil Trading Co. Flagged by both the Aleforge Special Drinkers Unit and the Providence Guard. Nobody knows why they are reaching out.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (The Southern Bellows Nation); VI (Stormveil Trading Co.)

groups.name: The Drunken Trials
groups.description: The Isles' most important cultural event: magic ale from the Tankard's spring that never hangs you over but does strange things at volume. Crowns the Liquor Kings. Tourism engine, prestige engine, and — since the MAA raided the first one — a standing target.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Drunken Trials); Concept I

groups.name: Owe Block Underground
groups.description: The district Providence's disparity built. Crimson Cutters, Seaside Circus, Wagwan's Stank Tank, underground markets, and quiet Veilwalker sympathizers (Sexton Gobbler's shrine). The obligatory tithe was cut to 25% after Gobbler's disgrace.
groups.loreSource: Compendium IV (Founding of Owe Block); Concept IV

groups.name: Veilwalkers of Fenwick
groups.description: The earth-born. Nature spirits made them from soil to resist the flesh-born; neither nature nor man should conquer the other. They trade in vows, not coin, curse the greedy with famine and disease, and play no politics — "you can't predict what don't want anything."
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers); VI (Veilwalker Trade & Custom)

groups.name: Unknownism (Baba Paku's Mission)
groups.description: The missionary strand of the unknown-gods faith that walked out of Owe Block with Baba Paku, "explaining to anyone who will listen the secrets of Providence's main religion." Wants its first Owe Block Saint. Funds itself with arms dealing.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (Baba Paku)

groups.name: Fayte Druids (Cloister Takeover)
groups.description: OPEN THREAD. The monks commandeered the Cloister months ago — the Kings' own meeting hall, built over a hole to hell and a beast's prison dimension. Strange chants and lights. Purpose unknown; every link to them is speculative by design.
groups.loreSource: Compendium XI (Open Mysteries); II (The Cloister)

groups.name: The Flesh-born (Humans)
groups.description: Humanity as a lineage bloc: the barbarians whose conquest the earth-born were made to resist, and every town since. The baseline against which every other lineage's standing is measured.
groups.loreSource: Compendium II (Fenwick & the Veilwalkers)

groups.name: Halfbreeds — the Line of Johns
groups.description: The only known human-Veilwalker line: John Cum (dead), John Rump (treasurer, holds the Cumstead), and plausibly Gideon Drake as distant ancestor. The Lagendale treaty template — fields blessed "so long as Walker blood remained in that family line" — is running again, live.
groups.loreSource: Compendium III (John Cum; John Rump); IV (The Rotted Soul — The First Treaty)

groups.name: Aleforge Tax Take
groups.description: Tolls, docking fees, property and luxury tax — the Analysis's preferred revenue (income tax is unenforceable when anyone can bury coin in a chest in the woods). Taxes force money out of circulation, steer behaviour, and fund the treasury. Drake zeroed sea tolls and raised road tolls 50%. 50 = today's mix.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (Taxes and Treasuries); Compendium III (Drake's policies)

groups.name: Aleforge Tariffs & Embargoes
groups.description: Mercantilism's first lever: aim for a positive balance of trade. Drake's cheap-grog import restriction, the 20% / 150% Veilwalker artifact tariff, and the tariff war with Providence where "each side [seeks] to choke the other's wealth." 50 = today.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy); Compendium II (Providence Foreign Relations)

groups.name: Patmos Tithe Rate
groups.description: The spire's cut. 50 = today: half of all earnings in Providence, a quarter in Owe Block since Gobbler's disgrace. The purest example of a treasury pulling coin out of pockets.
groups.loreSource: Compendium VI (The Church of Patmos); Concept IV

groups.name: Monopoly Charters
groups.description: Exclusive trade grants — a mercantilist government's favourite gift to its friends. Goldcoral is the obvious beneficiary; Roto was founded on the opposite principle.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy)

groups.name: Subsidized Industries
groups.description: Paying industries to outcompete rivals: Drake's wheat & barley subsidies and Gilded Tankard Grant, the Stewards-era guilds, Bonehardy's promised grain money, Buke's A.L.E. Financed, mostly, on Aleforge bond paper.
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy); Concept V

groups.name: Concept Performance Rewards
groups.description: Stock options or currency granted by the gamemaster to top performers after each concept — paid from the town treasury, never minted. "Consistent top performers will gain immense wealth, however this may come at political costs."
groups.loreSource: A Macroeconomic Analysis of the Pintland Isles (The Concept Economy)

relationships.short: the Kings now wear the mayor's chain
relationships.explanation: Bonehardy is a sitting Liquor King and the elected mayor — the Kings are no longer external heroes, their standing is the administration's standing, for better or worse.
relationships.precedent: Seamus Bonehardy elected mayor after the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: Bonehardy's record is every King's record
relationships.explanation: The entanglement cuts both ways: the administration's do-nothing calm (or any future fiasco) is laid at the whole Parliament's door, as the other Kings found when they publicly called Seamus out.
relationships.precedent: Bonehardy "has since done absolutely nothing in his tenure"

relationships.short: the Kings crush what they can see
relationships.explanation: When the Kings are strong they do what they have always done to prohibitionists: find the camp and clear it.
relationships.precedent: The cave massacre of the MAA; the raid on the MAMA camp beneath the abandoned shrine

relationships.explanation: Past a point, Kingly power stops deterring and starts recruiting. Every massacre left a mourner behind a rock — the MAA's left Maximilian, Maximilian's left MAMA. This is the Wronged Walker template: a grievance nobody bothers to resolve, returning later and larger.
relationships.precedent: MAA massacre → Maximilian; Maximilian's assassination → MAMA

relationships.explanation: MAMA's method is organized revolt timed for low morale, then blaming the Kings — Plinket's standing plan was to rise "if morale drops below 30% in any sector."
relationships.precedent: Plinket's revolt during the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: the Trials become a target again
relationships.explanation: Prohibitionists have always gone for the festival first; a stronger MAMA means guarded kegs, thinner crowds and nervous tourists.
relationships.precedent: The MAA raid on Aleforge during the first Drunken Trials

relationships.explanation: After their raid failed, the MAA waged guerrilla warfare "against the unsober people of Aleforge" — brewing is the economy they want dead.
relationships.precedent: MAA guerrilla campaign after the Drunken Trials

relationships.explanation: Plinket signed as "JR" precisely to shift suspicion onto the treasurer. Any MAMA resurgence drags John Rump's name back through the mud whether or not he did anything (he usually did something).
relationships.precedent: Plinket's pseudonym "Jathan Round (JR)"

relationships.short: militia and amnesty hold the line
relationships.explanation: A confident administration can do both halves of what kept MAMA down: Drake's volunteer militia and the Kings' amnesty deal.
relationships.precedent: Gideon's Aleforge Militia; the MAMA amnesty deal (Jagerbauhm the lone vote against)

relationships.explanation: Pirate freedom is an oppositional identity. The more the Kings look like an empire, the louder the Windsunk Council's "we end wars" posture and the more Aleforge youth sneak off to be pirates.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty on Aleforge: "fun at parties, dangerous with power"

relationships.short: a strong crown keeps an exile exiled
relationships.explanation: Drake was banished by the Kings' tribunal; his road back runs through their weakness, exactly as his first rise did while they were off celebrating the Cloister Beast.
relationships.precedent: Drake's election while the Kings "were nowhere to be seen"

relationships.short: the Kings are the Trials' headliners
relationships.explanation: The Trials crown Liquor Kings; famous Kings make the Trials famous. Their legend is the festival's marketing.
relationships.precedent: The six-way tie that began the Age of the Six Kings

relationships.short: Jack's purse is a King's purse
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral is privately owned by a sitting King; the Parliament's fortunes and Goldcoral's ships travel together (Cheeks fled to Providence on one).
relationships.precedent: Jack founds Goldcoral after the Last Pour; Cheeks' escape on a Goldcoral ship

relationships.explanation: Drake genuinely governed — the Barley Road, subsidies, the militia — and Aleforge once chose his "order and stability over the Liquor Kings' chaotic legacy." News of him moving takes a season or two to curdle into nostalgia at the castle.
relationships.precedent: Drake's mayoralty and the Stewards scandal

relationships.short: the exile makes the Kings look careless
relationships.explanation: Every rumour of Drake's scheming reads as the Kings' failure: they let him rise, then let him walk away alive.
relationships.precedent: Drake banished rather than executed after the Dread Harrow

relationships.explanation: "Extremism alienates moderate and decent discourse." Drake put down an MAA-inspired riot personally in his first days — then used a fake MAMA note to cover his own murder.
relationships.precedent: Drake on the front line of the inauguration riot; the staged MAMA note at Cum's body

relationships.explanation: Drake killed John Cum and is plausibly the Line of Johns' distant ancestor. A stronger Drake is an existential threat to Rump — or a claimant to whatever the blood is worth.
relationships.precedent: Cum's murder; the Corrupted Ancestry compass

relationships.explanation: The scandal that toppled Drake was letters to Roto's leadership about illegal trade in Factory artifacts. Drake with money means Roto's grey market with more stock.
relationships.precedent: The courier's letters that opened the Stewards of Aleforge

relationships.short: a steady Aleforge leaves no vacuum
relationships.explanation: Drake's pitch has always been "the Kings aren't here." A functioning mayoralty takes the pitch away.
relationships.precedent: Drake's original rise amid Thatcher's death and the Kings' absence

relationships.short: the Cardinal's voice is the law
relationships.explanation: In Providence religious authority *is* government: "his will the law of the land." Devotion converts straight into political control with no parliament in between.
relationships.precedent: Cardinal Addy commands from Patmos's spire

relationships.short: the church decrees what may be sold
relationships.explanation: The spire controls what may legally be crafted or sold; more control means more of the economy routed through Friars' market judgments and Sexton tithe-carts.
relationships.precedent: Friars judging the markets on Beastwatch

relationships.short: tithe gold funds the cryptic agenda
relationships.explanation: Half of all earnings flow into the church's coffers, "fueling a cryptic agenda" — tonic research, Kalifart towers, the red-earth bell. Money becomes ritual a season later.
relationships.precedent: The 50% tithe; the Kalifarts' search for a tonic to raise the dead

relationships.explanation: Whispered, unconfirmed: ClockHeart Tonic binds souls to Patmos's will. Past a threshold of devotion, social order stops being chosen and starts being dosed — the night-time revelry is the mask slipping.
relationships.precedent: Scholars' rumours that the tonic binds souls; Providence's dual day/night nature

relationships.explanation: Owe Block was founded out of Providence's religious and economic disparity. Tighten the tithe and the underclass district's informal economy expands to compensate; loosen it and money comes back above ground.
relationships.precedent: Founding of Owe Block; the tithe cut to 25% after Gobbler's disgrace

relationships.explanation: Extraction takes a season to become recruitment — the Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus fill their ranks from the tithe-broke.
relationships.precedent: A Walk on Owe Block: the gang wars

relationships.short: Friars clamp down on the district
relationships.explanation: Where the spire can enforce, underground culture goes quiet; when its grip slips, the Stank Tank gets loud.
relationships.precedent: Gobbler's purchased law enforcement hunting the Kings

relationships.short: order and the underground are zero-sum
relationships.explanation: Patmos social order and Owe Block culture are defined against each other — the district exists because the order has no room for it.
relationships.precedent: Founding of Owe Block

relationships.short: brewing tools out, red-earth mineral in
relationships.explanation: Roto is Providence's chief trade partner: brewing gear and rare tonic out, silks, spices and the red-earth mineral for the prayer bell in.
relationships.precedent: Providence Foreign Relations: Roto Kaishi

relationships.explanation: Goldcoral is headquartered in Providence and sells its profits to Providence's wealthy, who "only see what they want to see."
relationships.precedent: Goldcoral Incorporated

relationships.explanation: Aleforge tried a Patmos mayor once. Bronco Chestnut was "deeply unpopular and quickly voted out of office." Patmos zeal abroad reads as a threat at home.
relationships.precedent: Bronco Chestnut's mayoralty (the Long Thirst)

relationships.explanation: After Gobbler's hidden Veilwalker shrine, Addy "turned the scandal into doctrine." Orthodox strength means hunted shrines and Veil sympathizers keeping their heads down.
relationships.precedent: Sexton Gobbler's apostasy; the Day of Hollow Tongues

relationships.explanation: Baba Paku preaches the church's "secrets" to anyone who will listen; a vigilant spire does not appreciate its secrets being street-preached by an arms dealer.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku; the Day of Hollow Tongues

relationships.explanation: Patmos publicly preaches "order, sobriety, devotion." The prohibitionist current borrows that moral vocabulary — hypocrisy about the tonic notwithstanding.
relationships.precedent: Patmos public doctrine; Bronco Chestnut's theocratic push in Aleforge

relationships.explanation: Providence views the Trials as pagan excess and hosts its own solemn rites; a culturally ascendant Patmos draws pilgrims and prestige away from the festival.
relationships.precedent: Providence Foreign Relations: Aleforge

relationships.explanation: Rump's addiction runs on bootleg ClockHeart, still illegal in Providence where it is made. A tighter spire squeezes supply, and a squeezed addict with the treasury keys does something desperate.
relationships.precedent: Rump blackmails Bonehardy into legalizing bootleg tonic

relationships.explanation: A Patmos past its usual zeal hardens the Windsunk Council — Shanty remembers Providence as "a driftwood sermon by some tonic-made monk" and talks openly about cracking its lake port.
relationships.precedent: Jasper "no Eyes, all-Hands": "We call them next on the list."

relationships.explanation: Owe Block's gangs, bought police and hidden shrines are how Patmos control fails in practice.
relationships.precedent: Gobbler's corruption; the Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus

relationships.explanation: Unrest in Owe Block sends people to Aleforge looking for work outside Church control; they arrive as farmhands and mouths on a Cumstead already producing without its blessing.
relationships.precedent: Emergency Providence wheat deals during the blight; Guinnie's "blight blues"

relationships.explanation: Owe Block hides real Veilwalker sympathy — an obsidian-and-amethyst shrine behind a stone button in the Church of the Monk. When the district is culturally loud, the shrines get visitors.
relationships.precedent: The Veilwalker shrine found in A Walk on Owe Block

relationships.short: the district wants its first Saint
relationships.explanation: Unknownism is Owe Block's export; Baba Paku's ambition to be the first Owe Block Saint rides on the district's pride.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku

relationships.explanation: Baba Paku funds the mission with arms dealing. A booming mission is a booming gun trade.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku's "shady businesses such as arms dealing"

relationships.explanation: Every convert Baba Paku makes on a street corner is one who heard the church's secrets from an Owe Block arms dealer instead of from the spire.
relationships.precedent: Baba Paku

relationships.explanation: "They don't regulate us, we don't raid them." A stronger Windsunk Council leans on that balance.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: "a delicate, grizzled detente"

relationships.short: Roto's elite want the reefs "cleaned up"
relationships.explanation: Roto's merchant-lords have floated cleaning up the pirate factions on the outer reefs; a centralized Roto is the Council's nightmare.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: Current Tensions

relationships.short: pirates skip the cliffs for Roto
relationships.explanation: Easy Roto profits pull Shanty-born pirates straight past the cliffs, thinning the Council's crews.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Roto: pirates "chasing easier profits and softer landings"

relationships.explanation: Roto was built as the pirates' one reliable fence; a booming market pays better for what Shanty crews bring in.
relationships.precedent: Xi Jin Ping's floating shop

relationships.explanation: The Windsunk Council has murmured about hitting an Aleforge keg shipment "just to remind 'em who the sea belongs to."
relationships.precedent: Old Salty on Aleforge: Current Tensions

relationships.explanation: Shanty's drinking culture is half the Trials' audience and a steady supply of competitors; Aleforge's young "sneak off to become pirates" and come back for the festival.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty on Aleforge

relationships.explanation: Aleforge is a single-export state — the risk Drake tried to diversify away from with the Thatcher Scholarship. Brewing receipts are the tax base.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Brewers Tax and Thatcher Memorial Scholarship

relationships.explanation: A flush treasury funds the brewers — the Gilded Tankard Grant, the Kings' guilds, local barrel manufacture.
relationships.precedent: Gilded Tankard Grant; Stewards-era guilds and barrel localization

relationships.explanation: The festival runs on Tankard output; a strong brewing sector pays for bigger games.
relationships.precedent: Drunken Trials Revival Fund

relationships.explanation: Trials tourism is Aleforge's second export; festival crowds pay tolls, docking fees and luxury tax.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Revival Fund goal: "attract tourism during the games"

relationships.explanation: Aleforge's kegs "showin' up in towns far west" is the Trials' fame converted into orders.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty: "their festival's drawn more visitors than a sea-witch's curse"

relationships.short: the Trials are the Kings' mandate
relationships.explanation: The Kings' only formal legitimacy is having won the Trials. A revered festival is a revered crown.
relationships.precedent: Thatcher Sr. reinstating the annual Trials; the six-way tie

relationships.short: every Trials is a recruiting poster
relationships.explanation: The prohibitionists were born opposing "the culture of drinking that the Drunken Trials perpetuated"; the bigger the party, the better the sermon against it.
relationships.precedent: MAA founding; Maximilian's "20th anniversary" trap

relationships.short: real ale trade diverted to Roto books
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral routes real profit through Roto specifically to dodge scrutiny. As Jack's leverage grows, more of Aleforge's actual ale trade flows through Goldcoral's books rather than the town's brewers and treasury.
relationships.precedent: Jack seizes the Gilded Tankard's stockpile after Wepple's gambling losses

relationships.short: profits that never touch the treasury
relationships.explanation: Goldcoral "brings a lot of profits in but not much transparency" — the Wepple Ale sold at the Grog Galley pays no Aleforge brewers tax.
relationships.precedent: Wepple Ale sold in secret at Jack's Grog Galley

relationships.short: the original books live in Roto
relationships.explanation: All of Goldcoral's trade and its true ledgers run through Roto's low-regulation markets.
relationships.precedent: Goldcoral Incorporated

relationships.short: the robber baron buys a voice
relationships.explanation: Money becomes leverage: Bonehardy's campaign warned Jack would "leverage his position… to get better deals for his trade company."
relationships.precedent: Bonehardy's election remarks on Jack Anqoak

relationships.explanation: Jack ran for mayor on the Kings' "ungodly amounts of debt" and Rump's embezzlement; Goldcoral's political weight is opposition weight.
relationships.precedent: Jack Anqoak's mayoral election speech

relationships.short: taking too much from the earth
relationships.explanation: Aggressive mercantilism strips herbs, game and spirit-marked stones; those who "take too much from the earth" are haunted by famine and disease. The Veil's standing erodes first, the curse follows.
relationships.precedent: Young pirates plundering Fenwick lands; the Veilwalker curse

relationships.explanation: Opaque profits and secret stockpile sales mean trade no town can see or price; conversion rates drift.
relationships.precedent: Goldcoral's Roto-kept books

relationships.explanation: Bond confidence tracks whether the treasury can service Stewards-era debt.
relationships.precedent: The Aleforge Bond Market

relationships.explanation: The Kings issued later rounds "at increasingly unfavorable interest rates" precisely because the crisis looked unstable.
relationships.precedent: Stewards of Aleforge bond rounds

relationships.explanation: Roto traders were "especially happy to buy these bonds." An Aleforge debt scare is a hole in Roto's books.
relationships.precedent: Drake's bond issue; Roto's enthusiastic buying

relationships.explanation: When Roto is flush, it buys Aleforge debt; when it isn't, nobody else will.
relationships.precedent: The Aleforge Bond Market

relationships.explanation: Every town converts its sub-economy to Duckets for inter-town trade; a shaky Ducket makes Aleforge's export receipts worth less.
relationships.precedent: Economy Pitch: towns convert at story-driven rates

relationships.explanation: Roto is where Duckets change hands most; its margins live on stable rates.
relationships.precedent: Economy Pitch; Roto Kaiishi

relationships.explanation: Half of all Providence earnings convert into church coffers; a debased Ducket is a debased tithe.
relationships.precedent: The 50% tithe

relationships.explanation: Healthy Roto markets keep enough honest trade moving to hold the Ducket's value steady.
relationships.precedent: Roto as the Isles' trading hub

relationships.explanation: Roto traders once "flooded the market with cheap and disgusting grog"; Drake restricted grog imports to protect Aleforge's key export.
relationships.precedent: Drake's Roto Free Trade Deal and grog restrictions

relationships.explanation: Ale Beans and finished IPAs are coming north on illegal routes; disgusting or not, they compete for tankards — the Roto grog flood all over again.
relationships.precedent: SBN illegal trade routes; StormVeil partnership

relationships.explanation: The Ducket supply is meant to be flat. Smuggled trade with a nation outside every town's ledgers moves value nobody can see, and the rates drift a season later.
relationships.precedent: SBN smuggling; the Economy Pitch's flat-M2 rule

relationships.explanation: The Providence Guard has flagged the SBN — a state where "agnosticism is law" is doctrinal irritation for a theocracy.
relationships.precedent: SBN flagged by the Providence Guard

relationships.explanation: The Lagendale treaty template: the Veil blesses fields "so long as a human with Walker blood remained in that family line." The Cumstead's yield tracks how honoured that blood is — with a season's lag, like any harvest.
relationships.precedent: The First Treaty; John Cum's blessing

relationships.explanation: The blessing is the Veil's to give. Earth-born in good standing still tend the land that pleases them; diminished, they withdraw.
relationships.precedent: John Cum "spent years learning from the Veilwalkers"

relationships.explanation: Every mayor since Drake has promised the farmers money — Drake's wheat subsidies, Bonehardy's grain subsidies, Buke's A.L.E.
relationships.precedent: Barley and Wheat Subsidies; election speeches

relationships.explanation: John Rump is still Aleforge's treasurer, still addicted, still embezzling. The more secure his position, the more the ledger bleeds.
relationships.precedent: Mr. BBL's findings: Rump's confirmed embezzlement

relationships.explanation: Wheat is the Isles' staple input; failed harvests mean emergency imports paid out in Duckets.
relationships.precedent: Emergency Providence wheat deals during the blight

relationships.explanation: When the blight struck, Aleforge bought wheat from Providence. The Cumstead's loss is the spire's sale.
relationships.precedent: Stewards of Aleforge: emergency Providence wheat deals

relationships.explanation: The Veil was made to resist flesh-born conquest; flesh-born ascendancy is, by definition, the earth-born losing ground. Guinnie's "Veilwalker manifest destiny" vote is this edge in miniature.
relationships.precedent: The birth of the Veilwalkers; Guinnie's manifest-destiny vote

relationships.short: the earth takes back its due
relationships.explanation: Offend the Veil and "they'd just let the earth take us back" — famine and disease on those who take too much.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Fenwick

relationships.explanation: The Wronged Walker was dismissed because his case "crossed racial lines" and "made everyone uncomfortable." A flesh-born order sure of itself has little room for the half-blood.
relationships.precedent: The Wronged Walker's dismissal

relationships.explanation: The treaty made the halfbreed line the Veil's concern; earth-born standing lends the Johns theirs.
relationships.precedent: The First Treaty

relationships.short: custom is what keeps the Walkers whole
relationships.explanation: The Elders' law — the Vow of Mate, the refusal to spill Walker blood — is the Veil's cohesion. Strong custom, strong people.
relationships.precedent: The Vow of Mate; Veilwalker law

relationships.explanation: Veilwalker trade *is* religion: fishing gear for a promise to plant a flower. When the custom spreads, the faith deepens.
relationships.precedent: Veilwalker Trade & Custom

relationships.explanation: Gobbler was a Sexton. Veil devotion recruits from inside the spire's own ranks.
relationships.precedent: Sexton Gobbler's apostasy

relationships.short: the accord: wind when all winds fail
relationships.explanation: Pirates who keep the unspoken accord get healed, guided, and "sometimes gift[ed] with wind." A respected Veil is a luckier fleet.
relationships.precedent: Shanty Town on Fenwick: Political Balance

relationships.explanation: However the Druids' rites work, they are working from inside the Kings' seat. Devotion there is possession.
relationships.precedent: Fayte Druids commandeer the Cloister

relationships.short: the Kings' hall is not theirs
relationships.explanation: The Kings use the Cloister as their meeting hall and leave decisions to its magic lights. Someone else holding it is a humiliation and a lost instrument of power.
relationships.precedent: The Cloister: the Kings' meeting hall

relationships.short: the Kings could take it back
relationships.explanation: A strong Parliament has the swords to reclaim the Cloister.
relationships.precedent: The Cloister Beast storyline

relationships.explanation: Shanty's nightmare about the Cloister is specific: if its power wakes, the cliffs next door pay first. Past a point, Druid fervour starts emptying Shanty's taverns.
relationships.precedent: Old Salty: "If they unleash somethin'? It's our cliffs that'll catch the tide first."

relationships.explanation: Each season below par, coupons on the Stewards-era bonds come due and the treasury pays them. "The downside: they also accumulated significant national debt that they left for their successors."

relationships.short: the harvest sets the brewing season

relationships.explanation: The tithe isn't a one-off; each season of heavy extraction pushes more of Owe Block's life into the informal economy.
relationships.precedent: Founding of Owe Block

relationships.explanation: Leadership neutralized, base intact. Every season the belief persists above its floor, a few more people start meeting in caves.
relationships.precedent: MAMA "rendered inoperable" — ideology not eliminated

relationships.explanation: Roto traders reprice Aleforge bonds every season against the treasury's real position.

relationships.explanation: Embezzlement is a habit, not an event. As long as Rump keeps the treasury keys, the leak runs.
relationships.precedent: Rump "conveniently ignored in the chaos"

relationships.explanation: Without the blessing's bearer the Cumstead drifts toward whatever the blood's standing can sustain.
relationships.precedent: The blessing is "no longer applied" under Rump

relationships.short: the Grog Galley keeps selling Wepple Ale
relationships.explanation: The seized stockpile is sold in secret season after season — Aleforge's best brew, earning for Goldcoral.
relationships.precedent: Wepple Ale at Jack's Grog Galley

relationships.explanation: Drake is long-lived and patient. Whatever he gathers in Vodkonia turns into plans.
relationships.precedent: Drake "plotting his next moves" in Vodkonia

relationships.explanation: The last Keg of the year, every pirate gathers at the Tavern in peace. A strong ethos turns the feast into a show of Council strength.
relationships.precedent: Hoppy Holidays; the annual pirate gathering

relationships.explanation: Town currency exchanges run at set rates that update with story events; a shaky Ducket reprices every shelf in the Isles.

relationships.explanation: Taxes and wages flow into the treasury, which resets how much NPCs can spend each day and sizes the rotating town contracts. A rich Aleforge posts better work.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "Contracts… with fluctuating rewards based on the size of the town treasury"

relationships.short: Providence shops restock with the spire

relationships.explanation: Roto is where scarce goods come from when a town's own manufacturing falls short.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: shop availability depends on trade relations

relationships.explanation: The one way players push back up the chain: their buying and selling is velocity. Otherwise, players "have little to no impact on the Concept Economy."
relationships.precedent: Analysis: Player Economy vs. Concept Economy

relationships.short: too-fast money is inflation's other door
relationships.explanation: M2 times velocity is what chases the goods. Past a point, money changing hands faster than goods are made bids prices up even with a flat supply.
relationships.precedent: Analysis: "Duckets chase a limited supply of goods"

relationships.short: tolls and fees fill the treasury

relationships.explanation: Charters narrow who may sell; shoppers pay the difference.

events.name: The Fall of Lagendale
events.description: A farmer's forbidden union with a vow-bound Walker; the First Treaty blesses a bloodline's fields; the Wronged Walker's grievance is dismissed; Vodkonia is obliterated; the Rotted Soul rises as the first VeilRunner and is sealed by the River Coffin beneath what will become Hoegaarden.

events.name: Sackbeard Slays the Tavern Beast
events.description: Sackbeard's armada kills the great beast and builds the Tavern in its shell. Unrecorded: Sackbeard attacked a Veilwalker settlement for its nature-secrets, and first mate Gideon Drake killed him, cursed the crew with eternal life and banished them to the Nether.

events.name: Founding of Providence
events.description: The Monk Who Ne'er Slumber'd is exiled from Aleforge for hoarding ClockHeart Tonic and founds a city of perfect order on the cliffs.

events.name: Xi Jin Ping Founds Roto Kaiishi
events.description: The first ocean-bound shop, a fence for pirate plunder, grows into a seaborne nation-state run by hand-picked merchant-philosophers.

events.name: Founding of Owe Block
events.description: Providence's rigid hierarchy produces its own underclass district, with its own factions, economy and underground markets.

events.name: The Long Thirst
events.description: Aleforge governed by mayors without Kings. Bronco Chestnut's theocratic turn is voted out; Thatcher Sr. revives the annual Drunken Trials.

events.name: The Drunken Trials & the MAA Raid
events.description: The first-ever six-way tie begins the Age of the Six Kings. The MAA raid Aleforge to kill them and fail, falling back to guerrilla war.

events.name: The Cloister Beast & Thatcher's Death
events.description: The Kings kill the Cloister Beast, massacre the MAA in their cave (one child survives behind a rock), and forget to rescue Mayor Thomas Thatcher from Fentmaxxer's cage. He dies. The town's opinion of the Kings sours.

events.name: Gideon Drake Elected Mayor
events.description: Drake wins on order over chaos: Barley Road, wheat subsidies, Roto free-trade deal, Veilwalker artifact tariff, militia — and the first Aleforge Bonds.

events.name: The Liquor King Trials & Maximilian's Death
events.description: Maximilian Andrew Aldridge, the child who watched the MAA massacre, spends centuries in cryo-cycles building a hell for the Kings. Buke kills him. Not everyone calls it just — and MAMA is born.

events.name: A Walk on Owe Block: Gobbler Exposed
events.description: The Kings split into rival gangs, find a hidden Veilwalker shrine, and expose Sexton Gobbler's apostasy with the Veil Oath book and Chalice. The obligatory tithe falls to 25%. Addy turns the scandal into the Day of Hollow Tongues.

events.name: Stewards of Aleforge
events.description: The Kings govern: bonds at worsening rates, guilds, local barrels, emergency Providence wheat, legalized bootleg tonic (Rump's blackmail). Jack seizes the Tankard's stockpile. Drake murders John Cum and frames MAMA. Plinket unmasked; MAMA destroyed. The Dread Harrow comes through the portal; Jagerbauhm closes it. Drake banished to Vodkonia; Bonehardy elected mayor; Rump ignored.

events.name: Horror in Hoegaarden
events.description: The Kings breach the Rotted Soul's labyrinth and defeat him — releasing his soul into the world. The Line of Johns is revealed as half-Veilwalker. The conditions that create a VeilRunner are now known and replicable.

events.name: The Fayte Druids Take the Cloister
events.description: Monks commandeer the Kings' meeting hall. Strange chants and lights. Purpose unknown.

events.name: The Southern Bellows Make Contact
events.description: Illegal Ale Bean routes and a StormVeil partnership crack the SBN's generational isolation. Both the ASDU and the Providence Guard are watching.

hazards.name: VeilRunner Corruption Risk

inputs.note: the Elders' custom and the Vow of Mate holding
the halfbreed line honoured, not despised
an aggrieved part-Walker who has used Veil secrets to curse before

explanation.suppressedBy: Veilwalker law — the Vow of Mate, the refusal to spill Walker blood, the Elders' authority — and the Veil's general standing in the Isles.
explanation.erodedBy: Anything that pushes a Walker toward a broken vow and a dismissed grievance: flesh-born encroachment, contempt for the halfbreed line, and the Rotted Soul's released spirit, which knows exactly how to "disrupt the mating process."
explanation.ifCrossed: The Lagendale pattern repeats: a Vow of Mate is broken, the wronged party is dismissed, and a Walker draws magic from the earth to destroy instead of nurture. The first sign is always the soil.

omens: In Fenwick, a Walker has been seen standing very still at the edge of a field that has stopped growing.
The Night of the Earthen Veil is observed with unusual quiet this year.
Gregor Ashford, drunk, sings a verse about the 33rd Council that nobody taught him.

event.name: A Vow of Mate Is Broken
event.narrative: It began, as the Hoegaarden records say it always begins, with a grievance nobody wanted to hear. A Walker of Fenwick came before the Elders forsaken by a bonded mate — and the Elders, having apparently learned nothing from the 33rd Council, found the matter uncomfortable and sent him away. By the season's end three farms on the Brandywine edge had gone grey, the frogs had left the fen, and the Veilwalkers were seen in daylight, in number, looking for someone. The word "VeilRunner" is being spoken in Aleforge taverns by people who had to be told how to pronounce it.

wheat supply (a failed harvest means emergency imports)
Aleforge debt confidence (a distressed issuer is tempted to print)

taxes pulling coin out of circulation
banks paying interest they haven't earned from loans

explanation.suppressedBy: The closed loop: almost nothing may create Duckets, taxes pull coin back out of circulation into treasuries, and deep, honest Roto liquidity holds the conversion rates. The goal is M2 flat and velocity consistent.
explanation.erodedBy: Everything the Analysis warns about: big farms trading one item for endless coin, banks paying interest they never earned, a Roto currency black market, untracked outside money (SBN smuggling, Goldcoral's books), and a debt-strained town tempted to print.
explanation.ifCrossed: Somebody finds a way to mint. Rates between the towns' sub-economies come unstuck, and every treasury funded in Duckets discovers what its savings were really worth.

omens: Roto money-changers have started biting Duckets again.
A Shanty barkeep is refusing coin and asking for grog-weight.
Mr. BBL has been seen at the Post Office and Public Records, reading ledgers very slowly.

event.name: The Ducket Slips Its Moorings
event.narrative: No one admits to minting. Everyone admits that there are more Duckets than there were last season, and that a suspicious number of them smell faintly of Ale Bean. Conversion rates between Aleforge, Providence and Roto swing by the day; Roto's merchant-philosophers convene an emergency council whose only unanimous finding is that it was somebody else's fault. In Shanty Town, which never trusted coin, a barter economy of grog, rope and favours carries on almost smugly.

hazards.name: MAMA Radicalization

inputs.note: Kingly overreach (every massacre makes a mourner)
the Trials as a standing provocation

explanation.suppressedBy: Plinket's neutralization, the amnesty deal, the militia Drake built, and a calm, supported Bonehardy administration. In Goldsun, Providence's Day of Hollow Tongues also lets the Isles vent about the Kings harmlessly.
explanation.erodedBy: Kingly shows of force (the MAA massacre bred Maximilian; Maximilian's killing bred MAMA), bad harvests, an empty treasury — and every Drunken Trials, which is the thing they were founded to oppose.
explanation.ifCrossed: The Wronged Walker template in modern dress: the grievance the Kings never answered (was Maximilian's death an assassination?) returns with new leadership and a plan, not a riot.

omens: Pamphlets asking "WHO KILLED MAXIMILIAN?" have been nailed to the Hall of Ale.
Rollo reports that Susan has been writing a great many letters.
A child was seen in the cave under the abandoned shrine. Just watching.

event.name: MAMA Rises Again
event.narrative: The cells were "rendered inoperable," which, it turns out, is not the same as dead. A new voice — nobody knows whose; the letters are signed only "JR II," which John Rump considers deeply unfair — has stitched the surviving caves back together. They hit a brewery on Brewers Lane at dawn, leave the kegs untouched and the walls painted with a single question about Maximilian, and vanish. It is the restraint that frightens the castle.

hazards.name: Cumstead Collapse

inputs.note: subsidy money for farmhands and seed
Rump's grip (an addict running a farm)
a Veil still willing to tend the soil

explanation.suppressedBy: Whatever yield the unblessed Cumstead can still manage, subsidy money, and the Veil's residual goodwill toward the Line of Johns.
explanation.erodedBy: John Rump's neglect, contempt for the halfbreed line, and the green Factory sludge nobody has cleaned out of Cum's fields.
explanation.ifCrossed: The Cumstead fails outright, not a poor year but a dead one, and Aleforge learns how much of its economy was a Veilwalker blessing on one sad man.

omens: Farmhands say the green sludge has come back along the north furrows.
John Rump has sold two ploughs. Nobody knows to whom.
The scarecrow at the Cumstead has been found facing the house.

event.name: The Cumstead Fails
event.narrative: The wheat came up grey and went down black. Farmhands found the green Factory sludge seeping from the same north furrows Mr. BBL noted during the Commission, and John Rump — reached for comment at a tonic den — asked whether the harvest "had to be this season specifically." Aleforge signs another emergency grain deal with Providence at a price the Cardinal described as merciful. The brewers of Brewers Lane start measuring malt with spoons.

hazards.name: Aleforge Bond Crisis

inputs.note: insurgency risk priced into the paper

explanation.suppressedBy: Roto's continued willingness to hold Aleforge paper, and a treasury that can still make its coupons.
explanation.erodedBy: Stewards-era debt at "increasingly unfavorable" rates, an embezzling treasurer, and a mayor whose signature achievement is inaction.
explanation.ifCrossed: Aleforge misses a coupon. Roto, holding the paper, stops being a partner and starts being a creditor.

omens: Roto brokers are quoting Aleforge bonds by the barrel rather than the Ducket.
The treasury ledger has three pages glued together.
Mr. BBL's posture has become noticeably tense.

event.name: Aleforge Misses a Coupon
event.narrative: The coupon came due on Mooringday and the treasury, after a thorough search of the castle, the Boner Bar and John Rump's coat, could not find it. Roto's merchant-philosophers — the largest holders — issue a statement of great philosophical depth that amounts to "pay us." Goldcoral quietly buys distressed Aleforge paper at a tenth of its face. Bonehardy addresses the town and says, of the crisis, nothing at all, which for once is noticed.

hazards.name: Owe Block Rising

inputs.note: an informal economy that still feeds people

explanation.suppressedBy: The spire's enforcement and the 25% tithe concession the district won after Gobbler.
explanation.erodedBy: Tithe pressure, gang recruitment, and Baba Paku's side business in arms.
explanation.ifCrossed: Owe Block stops being Providence's problem district and becomes its rival city.

omens: Wagwan has closed the Stank Tank early three nights running.
Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus colours were seen at the same table.
The Owe Block Chronicle has stopped printing the Cardinal's prayer times.

event.name: The Owe Block Rising
event.narrative: It started with a Sexton's tithe cart overturned on the Stank Tank's corner and ended, three Kegs later, with Crimson Cutters and Seaside Circus standing on the same barricade — a sight Wagwan called "worse than the Kings splitting my bar in half." The Friars withdraw above the lower terraces. Someone reopens the shrine behind the stone button in the Church of the Monk, and this time there is a queue.

hazards.name: Credit Crunch

inputs.note: deposits fleeing to the night market

explanation.suppressedBy: Banks with real loan income, underwriters with reserves, and Aleforge paper that still trades near par.
explanation.erodedBy: Wreck seasons, Aleforge bond stress, and interest paid out of thin air. The credit market is young, and so are its reserves.
explanation.ifCrossed: The underwriters fold, the banks call in their loans, and the people who were promised ships and shops on credit find out the credit was a wager.

omens: Roto bookmakers are offering odds on whether the insurers themselves will return.
A holdings account in Aleforge paid its interest in IOUs this Keg.
Three ship loans were called in the same week.

event.name: The Underwriters Fold
event.narrative: It took one bad Stormtide and three missing hulls. The Roto gamblers who had been writing voyage policies discovered, in rapid succession, that they were insurers, that they were insolvent, and that they had borrowed the reserves from the banks. The banks call in every ship and shop loan on the books; half-built storefronts in Aleforge stand empty with the scaffolding still up. Goldcoral buys the distressed policies for a song and is, somehow, the only party that comes out ahead.

hazards.name: Cloister Stirring

inputs.note: Kings able to take their hall back
the Veil's old stewardship of the land

explanation.suppressedBy: The Cloister Beast is dead and the Kings still have the strength to evict squatters from their own hall.
explanation.erodedBy: The Fayte Druids' unexplained chanting, in a building over a hole to hell, over a prison dimension, next to the magic lights that decide fates. Veilfrost is when things best left alone tend to stir.
explanation.ifCrossed: OPEN THREAD — the simulator only knows the shape: something under the Cloister answers, and Shanty Town's cliffs catch the tide first.

omens: The lights in the Cloister hillside have been seen from Shanty Town, in a colour nobody can name.
The Druids' chanting now carries to the Tavern on still nights.
A second invisible hallway is rumoured. The Kings have not checked.

event.name: The Cloister Lights Answer
event.narrative: On the longest night of Veilfrost, the magic lights in the Cloister hillside — the ones the Kings consult when they cannot be bothered to decide — all lit at once and stayed lit. The Druids' chant stopped. Whatever they were asking, they have been answered, and they are not saying what the answer was. Shanty Town reports a warm tide, the smell of sulphur, and three ships that sailed out to look and came back with their crews insisting it was a lovely evening.

hazards.name: Ashen Oath Purge

inputs.note: the prohibitionist current emboldening the Oath

explanation.suppressedBy: A proud, grog-soaked pirate culture and a Windsunk Council strong enough to toss fanatics off the cliffs.
explanation.erodedBy: Anything that spreads the idea that grog has tainted the world, and anything that thins the crews who would stand against it.
explanation.ifCrossed: The Ashen Oath stops abducting one person a year and starts burning the Shoals.

omens: A second charred effigy was found on the cliffs this Keg, and it is not the Night of the False Sun.
Someone has been pouring grog into the sea at the Tavern steps.

event.name: The Ashen Oath Burns the Shoals
event.narrative: The Night of the False Sun came early and stayed. The Ashen Oath set the grog stores along La-Di-Da Street alight, tried to burn the beast bones, and left the Windsunk Council arguing over whether this counts as a raid. Half the captains sailed out rather than choose a side.

hazards.name: Roto Succession Crisis

inputs.note: a big player wanting to pick the heir
money that prefers a weak heir

explanation.suppressedBy: Xi's personally trained chain of heirs and the culture of principles around it.
explanation.erodedBy: The biggest players wanting a say in the next heir, exactly what Xi built the system to prevent.
explanation.ifCrossed: "One poorly chosen candidate could be the end of Roto." A poorly chosen candidate is chosen.

omens: Two merchant houses are each training a "true" disciple of Xi.
A Goldcoral ship has been moored at the council stilts for three Kegs.

event.name: A Poorly Chosen Heir
event.narrative: The heir took the council seat with Goldcoral's blessing and three new laws in his first week, none with any clear economic benefit. The old taboos stop holding; the night market opens at noon.

hazards.name: The Veil Withdraws

explanation.suppressedBy: Promises kept to the Veil, and islanders who "give due respect to the earth."
explanation.erodedBy: Taking too much from the earth, and a flesh-born majority that stops leaving offerings at the treeline.
explanation.ifCrossed: The Veil stops trading vows and stops tending the soil. No curse, just absence, which is worse.

omens: The fishing lures from Fenwick have stopped arriving.
A pirate who left an offering at the treeline found it there untouched a week later.

event.name: The Veil Withdraws
event.narrative: Fenwick did not curse anyone. The Walkers simply stopped trading vows, stopped guiding travellers, and stopped tending the fields at the forest edge. By the end of the season nobody could find the village at all.

injectables.name: Gideon Drake makes a move from Vodkonia
injectables.narrative: A Vodkonian skiff reaches Shanty Town carrying exotic rum, no crew, and a letter in Drake's hand addressed to "the people of Aleforge, who deserved better."

injectables.name: The Rotted Soul's released spirit resurfaces
injectables.narrative: Hoegaarden's night archivist reports the Corrupted Ancestry compass spinning, then stopping — pointing, very steadily, toward Aleforge.

injectables.name: A new VeilRunner emerges
injectables.narrative: The thing the Hoegaarden records warned was replicable is replicated.

injectables.name: A MAMA cell reactivates
injectables.narrative: Someone has been restocking the cave under the abandoned shrine. The Kings raided it once already; nobody filled it in.

injectables.name: The Fayte Druids reveal their purpose
injectables.narrative: The Druids open the Cloister doors for the first time in months and invite the Kings to "witness." The Kings, hungover, send Rollo.

injectables.name: A second Tome Monument is found
injectables.narrative: A second of the six Tome Monuments surfaces; Hoegaarden, Roto relic-brokers and at least one Liquor King all claim to have found it first.

injectables.name: John Rump's embezzlement is finally prosecuted
injectables.narrative: Mr. BBL's old Commission files are dusted off. Rump is arrested at a tonic den; the question of who runs the Cumstead now has no good answer.

injectables.name: Cardinal Addy restores the full tithe in Owe Block
injectables.narrative: From the spire, the Cardinal announces that the Gobbler-era concession has served its purpose. The tithe returns to half of all earnings.

injectables.name: Bonehardy issues a new round of Aleforge Bonds
injectables.narrative: In his first recorded act as mayor, Bonehardy signs a new bond issue. Roto buys, at a rate described by Mr. BBL as "brave."

injectables.name: The Southern Bellows open formal trade
injectables.narrative: A steam glider lands at Aleforge customs carrying the Pale's seal and a crate of IPAs so bitter the harbourmaster weeps.

injectables.name: A legendary Drunken Trials
injectables.narrative: The Trials run three days over; the spring's ale produces visions in two competitors and a marriage proposal to a goat.

injectables.name: The Dread Harrow's portal flickers
injectables.narrative: For one night, the harbour water where the Dread Harrow materialized glows green. Drake, it is remembered, spent twenty years afraid of exactly this.

injectables.name: The Kings publicly feud over Bonehardy's inaction
injectables.narrative: Jack, Guinnie and Buke denounce the mayor at the Hall of Ale. Bonehardy does not respond, which his supporters call "statesmanlike."

injectables.name: A mega-farm floods the exchange
injectables.narrative: Someone has built a wheat farm the size of a parish and is selling its entire output to the Aleforge exchange every day at the posted rate — the exact thing the Analysis said must never be allowed.

injectables.name: Roto's currency black market booms
injectables.narrative: After dark on the lower stilts of Roto, a Ducket is now worth whatever the man with the lantern says, and more people are asking him than asking the exchange.

injectables.name: Aleforge embargoes Providence goods
injectables.narrative: Bonehardy signs an embargo on Providence brewing tools, reportedly without reading it. Shoppers notice the prices before they notice the policy.

injectables.name: The Kings are paid their concept performance rewards
injectables.narrative: The gamemaster's ledger closes on another concept and the treasury pays out the Kings' performance rewards in coin and Goldcoral stock. Jack's share is the largest; nobody is surprised.

injectables.name: Foreign coin arrives from outside the Isles
injectables.narrative: A StormVeil Albatross unloads a hold of Bellows coin at Roto — the one legitimate way new money can enter the Isles, and a test of whether anyone is counting.

injectables.name: A season of wrecks
injectables.narrative: Four merchantmen go down off the Shoals in a single Keg. The underwriters pay; Shanty Town's salvagers, who were somehow already out there, do very well.

injectables.name: The first Bank of Aleforge opens its lending window
injectables.narrative: A bank opens beside the Hall of Ale offering loans for ships, shops and land, and holdings accounts that pay interest from somewhere, allegedly loan income.

Stormtide: Stormtide batters the coasts; captains who can read the sky stay in port, and the ones who can't become Shanty Town's newest residents.
The wet season rolls in, the Gae Strait turns ugly, and Aleforge readies the Trials grounds while Providence readies its disapproval.
Stormtide: dangerous seas, overflowing gutters, and the annual feast in Aleforge, where the spring's ale does its strange work.
Goldsun: Goldsun brings calm seas and full sails, and every merchant in Roto suddenly remembers who owes them money.
The dry season: Beer Day in Shanty Town, Liquor Day everywhere, and the Day of Hollow Tongues in Providence, where rumours about the Kings are written down and blessed.
Goldsun opens on Brewmasters Day, the ale fountain in Aleforge's square running as it has since the Deity's blessing.
Veilfrost: Veilfrost: a hundred and seventeen days of night. The Veilwalkers walk, and things best left alone begin to stir.
The long dark falls. Fenwick keeps the Night of the Earthen Veil; the Ashen Oath keeps the Night of the False Sun, and Aleforge lights its pipes across the bay.
Veilfrost settles over the Isles; mystical anomalies spike, the Unholy Pilgrimage staggers bar to bar, and the year ends with the Hoppy Holidays at Sackbeard's.

closers.text: Mayor Bonehardy, asked to comment on the season, did absolutely nothing, to broad public approval.
Mayor Bonehardy's approval is now being discussed in the same tone as the Long Thirst.
Somewhere in Roto, a merchant-philosopher reprices Aleforge paper and does not bother telling anyone.
MAMA remains, officially, "rendered inoperable." Rollo reports Susan still writes a lot of letters.
John Rump was seen at the Cumstead exactly once this season, briefly, looking for something he had hidden in the barn.
Jack Anqoak's Grog Galley posts its best season yet; the Gilded Tankard's former owner pours every drink.
In Providence the Apostles have stopped blinking, which the Cardinal describes as devotion.
Fenwick is quieter than usual. The pirates have started leaving bigger offerings at the treeline.
Letters postmarked from nowhere are circulating in Aleforge, all in the same fine hand.
Aleforge shopkeepers report customers who are "just looking," which the Chronicle has declared a recession.
Town shops restock a little slower every Keg; nobody can say why, only that everything costs more.
After dark in Roto, a Ducket is worth whatever the man with the lantern says it is.
Roto bookmakers are offering odds on whether the insurers themselves will return.
The Kings' performance bonuses were paid on time, which is more than can be said for the bond coupons.
The Duckets in circulation are, for once, exactly as many as there were last season. Somewhere, an economist weeps with joy.
Rollo changed boyfriends twice this season, which analysts agree had no macroeconomic effect.
Wepple is, allegedly, still working on a new brew in secret.
Cumsock the goat remains a fixture of the administration.
Gregor Ashford was too drunk to play again, but somehow knew the words to a song from before Lagendale fell.
The Aleforge Chronicle ran eleven stories on Mr. BBL's posterior and one on the economy.

openThreads.name: The Rotted Soul's released spirit
openThreads.summary: Defeated in Hoegaarden, but his soul is loose, and the recipe for a VeilRunner is now known and repeatable.

openThreads.name: Gideon Drake in Vodkonia
openThreads.summary: Banished, long-lived, aggrieved, and plotting from unexplored shores.

openThreads.name: John Rump holds the Cumstead
openThreads.summary: No Veilwalker blessing, an addict in charge, and Factory sludge in the furrows.

openThreads.name: MAMA's surviving cells
openThreads.summary: Plinket is neutralized; the ideology and some cells are not.

openThreads.name: The Fayte Druids in the Cloister
openThreads.summary: Chants and lights in the Kings' own meeting hall. Purpose unknown.

openThreads.name: The Rotted Soul's living descendant
openThreads.summary: The Corrupted Ancestry compass points at someone alive. The half-blood Line of Johns is the obvious suspect.

openThreads.name: The Southern Bellows reach out
openThreads.summary: Generations of isolation cracking through smuggling and StormVeil. Nobody knows why now.

openThreads.name: The Tome Monuments
openThreads.summary: One of six found. What the other five hold is unknown.
